proposals.before: Yin memorialized; Zhaozong refused. Days later the Founder asked again. Zhu Wen said: “I would never dare raise a hand—Yin is trying to sell me out.”
proposals.after: Yin memorialized; Zhaozong refused. Another day Zhaozong asked the Founder about it. Zhu Wen said: “I would never dare raise a hand—Yin is trying to sell me out.”
proposals.reason: Chinese 佗日以問太祖 continues from 昭宗不許: Zhaozong questioned Taizu; Taizu’s reply 臣安敢及之 is addressed to the emperor, not a case of Taizu asking again.

proposals.before: Yin memorialized it; Zhaozong would not consent. Another day the Founder asked again. The Founder said: “How would your servant dare touch this? Yin means to sell me out.”
proposals.after: Yin memorialized it; Zhaozong would not consent. Another day he asked the Founder. The Founder said: “How would your servant dare touch this? Yin means to sell me out.”
proposals.reason: 以問太祖 means the subject asked Taizu. The continuing subject is Zhaozong, whose refusal immediately precedes the clause.

proposals.before: At the move to Luoyang Zhaozong told Jiang Xuanhui: “De is my beloved son. Why does Quanzhong want him dead?”
proposals.after: At the move to Luoyang Zhaozong told Jiang Xuanhui: “The Prince of De is my beloved son. Why does Quanzhong want him dead?”
proposals.reason: 德王 is the Prince of De, not the clipped English name De, which obscures that Zhaozong is naming his enfeoffed son.

proposals.before: Eunuch Liu Jishu plotted to depose Zhaozong. His nephew Xiyin came through embassy clerk Cheng Yan to Zhen: “The emperor has turned cruel and kills without cause. The chief eunuch fears for his neck and will depose him. Will you and the clerks act together to settle the court—yes or no?”
proposals.after: Eunuch Liu Jishu plotted to depose Zhaozong. His nephew Xizheng came through embassy clerk Cheng Yan to Zhen: “The emperor has turned cruel and kills without cause. The chief eunuch fears for his neck and will depose him. Will you and the clerks act together to settle the court—yes or no?”
proposals.reason: Chinese 希正 is Xizheng; the idiomatic Xiyin does not match the given characters.

proposals.before: The Founder was fighting between Xing and Ming. Jishu forged a retired-emperor edict to him. Zhu Wen wavered. Zhen said: “The disorders of Shufan and Yili became the stuff from which hegemons are made.
proposals.after: The Founder was fighting between Xing and Ming. Jishu forged a retired-emperor edict to him. Zhu Wen wavered. Zhen said: “The disorders of Shu Diao and Yili became the stuff from which hegemons are made.
proposals.reason: 豎刁 is the Qi eunuch Shu Diao, not Shufan; the allusion is otherwise unintelligible.

proposals.before: When Pei Ji of the Works ran the Finance Commission he took Di as touring inspector.
proposals.after: When Pei Qu of the Works ran the Finance Commission he took Di as touring inspector.
proposals.reason: Chinese 裴璩 is Pei Qu; Ji does not match 璩.

proposals.before: Fan delivered Zongquan to Zhu Wen. The Founder wanted the triumph loud and asked to present the captive at Tang court. Tang answered that Shi Pu, when he broke Huang Chao, had sent only severed ears—Zongquan was not worth a grand presentation. Remonstrance official Xu Yanqiu also asked that he be executed on the spot.
proposals.after: Fan delivered Zongquan to Zhu Wen. The Founder wanted the triumph loud and asked to present the captive at Tang court. Tang answered that Shi Pu, when he broke Huang Chao, had sent only severed ears—Zongquan was not worth a grand presentation. Remonstrance official Xu Yanshu also asked that he be executed on the spot.
proposals.reason: 徐彥樞 is Xu Yanshu (樞), not Yanqiu.

proposals.before: Taizu feared the warlords would turn on him while he was weak. He nudged Du Hong, Zhong Chuan, Wang Shinan, Qian Liu, and the rest to name him commander-in-chief and to let him hold Yan Prefecture as well.
proposals.after: Taizu feared the warlords would turn on him while he was weak. He nudged Du Hong, Zhong Chuan, Wang Shifan, Qian Liu, and the rest to name him commander-in-chief and to let him hold Yan Prefecture as well.
proposals.reason: 王師範 is the same Wang Shifan named earlier in this chapter; Shinan is a wrong romanization.

proposals.before: He was orphaned early and wound up in Bian Prefecture. A wealthy man named Li Ranglan bought him in the slave market and raised him as his own.
proposals.after: He was orphaned early and wound up in Bian Prefecture. A wealthy man named Li Rang obtained him and raised him as his own.
proposals.reason: 李讓 is the personal name; 闌得之 is the verb (got/obtained him), not a fused name Li Ranglan.

proposals.before: When Taizu held Xuanyi he adopted Li Rang. Xun took the Zhu surname for himself.
proposals.after: When Taizu held Xuanwu he adopted Li Rang. Xun took the Zhu surname for himself.
proposals.reason: 宣武 is Xuanwu Circuit, not Xuanyi.

proposals.before: Later Liang attacked Wu and Pang Shigu fell at Qingkou. Broken troops straggled home through Ying in blinding snow, starving and freezing. Jingrao stacked firewood along the Huai and cooked porridge for them; many lived because of it. Taizu named him acting governor of Wuning, then military commissioner.
proposals.after: Afterwards Liang troops attacked Wu and Pang Shigu fell at Qingkou. Broken troops straggled home through Ying in blinding snow, starving and freezing. Jingrao stacked firewood along the Huai and cooked porridge for them; many lived because of it. Taizu named him acting governor of Wuning, then military commissioner.
proposals.reason: 其後梁兵攻吳 means afterwards Liang troops attacked Wu; 其後 is the adverb, not the dynasty name 後梁.

proposals.before: Ying bordered Huainan West and Qin Zongquan struck again and again. Jingrao fought him off. Zongquan swallowed every Henan prefecture but could not take Ying, and people from the surrounding districts fled to Jingrao for safety.
proposals.after: Ying bordered Huaixi (Huai West) and Qin Zongquan struck again and again. Jingrao fought him off. Zongquan swallowed every Henan prefecture but could not take Ying, and people from the surrounding districts fled to Jingrao for safety.
proposals.reason: 淮西 is Huaixi, the Huai-west circuit, not Huainan West (淮南).

decisions.reason: 佗日以問太祖 continues from 昭宗不許, so Zhaozong asked Taizu; 太祖曰「臣安敢及之」 is a servant’s reply to the emperor. The prior “the Founder asked again” reverses asker and addressee.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 昭宗不許，佗日以問太祖，太祖曰：「臣安敢及之

decisions.reason: 以問太祖 marks Taizu as the one questioned; the zero subject carries from 昭宗不許. “The Founder asked again” invents the wrong agent.
德王 is the title Prince of De; clipping to “De” drops the enfeoffment title Zhaozong uses for his son.
希正 romanizes as Xizheng; Xiyin does not match the characters.
豎刁 is the Qi eunuch Shu Diao; Shufan is a mistransliteration that breaks the Spring-and-Autumn allusion.
裴璩 is Pei Qu; Ji does not correspond to 璩.
徐彥樞 ends in 樞 (shu); Yanqiu misreads the given name.
王師範 is Wang Shifan; Shinan is a wrong romanization of 範.
李讓 is the personal name and 闌得之 the verb phrase “obtained him”; Li Ranglan and “bought him in the slave market” fuse and invent beyond the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 富人李讓闌得之，養以為子

decisions.reason: 宣武 is Xuanwu Circuit; Xuanyi misreads 武.
其後 is temporal “afterwards,” and 梁兵攻吳 names Liang troops; “Later Liang” wrongly treats 其後梁 as the dynasty 後梁.
淮西 is Huaixi (Huai West), distinct from 淮南; Huainan West conflates the two circuits.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0004 shows English Xiyin came only from misreading 希正; the correct personal-name claim remains c0129 Xizheng.
Accepted r0005 shows Shufan was created solely by the bad romanization of 豎刁; the correct personal-name claim remains c0142 Shu Diao.
Accepted r0006 shows Pei Ji came only from misreading 裴璩; the correct personal-name claim remains c0194 Pei Qu.
Accepted r0007 shows Xu Yanqiu came only from misreading 彥樞; the correct personal-name claim remains c0239 Xu Yanshu.
Accepted r0008 shows Wang Shinan came only from misreading 王師範; the correct personal-name claim remains c0207 Wang Shifan.
Accepted r0009 shows Li Ranglan fused the name 李讓 with the verb 闌得之; the correct personal-name claim remains c0260 Li Rang.
Accepted r0009 removes the invented slave-market purchase; 闌得之 does not state a purchase, so purchased-dependent has no source support.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0009 keeps the adoption by Li Rang but drops “bought,” which the bad idiomatic alone supplied for 闌得之.
